queer_characters.name: Tom Collins
queer_characters.notes: Described as a gay anarchist philosophy professor living with AIDS; part of a central, loving relationship with Angel.

queer_characters.name: Angel Dumott Schunard
queer_characters.notes: A drag queen and street musician in a loving relationship with Collins; portrayed warmly but dies from AIDS, contributing to a tragic arc.
queer_characters.contest_notes: Source describes Angel as a 'drag queen' and Collins's partner but does not specify Angel's gender identity; readings vary between a gay man doing drag and a more expansive gender-nonconforming/trans interpretation. Source text does not resolve this.

queer_characters.name: Maureen Johnson
queer_characters.notes: Described explicitly as a bisexual performance artist, currently in a relationship with Joanne.

queer_characters.name: Joanne Jefferson
queer_characters.notes: Described explicitly as a lesbian, Harvard-educated lawyer and Maureen's girlfriend.

contributor_notes: Identities for Collins, Maureen, and Joanne are explicit in the provided plot text. Angel is described as a drag queen and Collins's partner, so tagged 'gay' provisionally; the source does not state Angel's gender identity, so this is flagged as contested for a maintainer to review. Angel's death from AIDS could arguably fit a 'bury-your-gays'/'tragic-queer' framing, but I did not tag it because the source frames AIDS as a central historical theme rather than gratuitous; a maintainer should decide with fuller context. No subtitle or audio-language info was provided. 'found-family' inferred from the bohemian ensemble framing but should be verified.
